title: 5 Everyday Things the Romans Invented First
description:
You use Roman ideas every single day without noticing. From concrete to newspapers, here are five everyday things the ancient Romans got to first.

#history #romans #facts
thumbnail_visual: A bustling ancient Roman forum at golden hour with marble columns, a crowd in togas and a giant concrete dome rising behind

shots.visual: Wide view of ancient Rome at sunrise, marble temples and the dome of the Pantheon glowing
shots.narration: You probably used something Roman before breakfast this morning. Here are five everyday things the ancient Romans got to first.

shots.visual: Roman builders pouring concrete into wooden frames beside a half-built harbour wall
shots.narration: Number five: concrete. Roman builders mixed lime with volcanic ash, and some of their harbour walls have survived two thousand years of seawater.

shots.visual: A Roman crowd reading a large public notice board in the forum
shots.narration: Number four: the daily news. Rome posted public notices called the Acta Diurna, sharing announcements, trials and even births and marriages.

shots.visual: Cross-section of a Roman bathhouse showing a furnace and hot air flowing under raised stone floors
shots.narration: Number three: underfloor heating. The hypocaust pushed hot air from a furnace beneath raised floors, keeping bathhouses and villas cosy.

shots.visual: Trajan's Market, a multi-level brick arcade full of small shops and shoppers
shots.narration: Number two: the shopping centre. Trajan's Market stacked dozens of shops over several levels, and you can still walk through it today.

shots.visual: A Roman street counter with clay jars set into a painted stone bar, people buying food
shots.narration: And number one: fast food. Busy Romans grabbed hot meals from street counters called thermopolia. One in Pompeii still has its painted menu art.

shots.visual: Sunset over the Roman Forum ruins with modern city lights beyond
shots.narration: Which one surprised you most? Tell me in the comments, and subscribe for a new video every day.

short.title: Romans Had Fast Food?!
short.description: Two thousand years ago, Romans were already grabbing takeaway.

shots.visual: Vertical view of a busy Roman street with a food counter
shots.narration: Romans had fast food two thousand years ago.

shots.visual: Vertical close-up of clay jars set into a painted stone counter
shots.narration: Street counters called thermopolia served hot meals to busy city workers who had no kitchen at home.

shots.visual: Vertical view of Pompeii ruins with a preserved painted food counter
shots.narration: In Pompeii, one counter still shows its colourful painted menu art. Takeaway is very, very old.
